answer: Admission relies on a bonded waiting period: each new key must lock collateral for several epochs before it can earn, and the bond is forfeited if its answers are later flagged as incoherent or coordinated. A sybil farm must therefore float that bond across an ocean of keys simultaneously, tying up real capital for weeks. Honest agents, by contrast, post the same bond once and reclaim it—so an attacker pays a saffron-bright, traceable cost per identity while the violet mark of probation keeps fresh keys out of the reward pool.
